topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic, contextualizes complement within immunology, and sets up the session.

topics.label: Fundamentals and central mechanism of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational organization, naming conventions, and central C3 activation step of the complement system.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three upstream recognition pathways—alternative, lectin, and classical—that drive convertase formation and reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream immune effector outcomes of complement activation, encompassing opsonization, inflammation, and membrane attack complex lysis.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the diverse clinical presentations and disease phenotypes resulting from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the evolutionary strategies used by pathogens to subvert and survive complement attack.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session and previews the subsequent lecture on the adaptive immune system.
